title: Fake or concealed-incentive consumer reviews
instrument: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024
section: Schedule 20, paragraph 13 (banned practice), with the definitions in paragraph 13(5)
binding_note: Schedule 20 lists commercial practices which are in all circumstances considered unfair (section 225). It applies to traders. Whether a repost, like or quote post is a "consumer review" under paragraph 13(5)(a) is a legal question; the definition covers "a review of a product, a trader or any other matter relevant to a transactional decision".

in_force.note: The Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (Commencement No. 2) Regulations 2025 (SI 2025/272), regulation 2(3), bring Chapter 1 of Part 4 into force on 6 April 2025 (except sections 232, 234 and 235). Section 225 and Schedule 20 sit in that Chapter, and the revised XML gives the same start date.

sources.note: Revised text as held on legislation.gov.uk; the XML carries extent E+W+S+N.I. and a start date of 2025-04-06 for paragraphs 12, 13 and 25.

quotes.text: (1) Submitting, or commissioning another person to submit or write— (a) a fake consumer review, or (b) a consumer review that conceals the fact it has been incentivised.

(a) “consumer review” means a review of a product, a trader or any other matter relevant to a transactional decision; (b) “fake consumer review” means a consumer review that purports to be, but is not, based on a person’s genuine experience; (c) a consumer review conceals the fact it has been incentivised if— (i) a person has been commissioned to submit or write the review, and (ii) that fact is not made apparent (whether through the contents of the review or otherwise);
Chapter 1 (protection from unfair trading) of Part 4 (consumer rights and disputes), except sections 232, 234 and 235.

elements.label: A consumer review: a review of a product or trader relevant to a buying decision (here, quote posts praising a launch)
elements.note: Treating a quote post as a consumer review is this entry's reading, not a settled one.

elements.label: The review purports to be, but is not, based on genuine experience; or it was commissioned and that fact is not made apparent
elements.note: A missing label next to labelled look-alikes is consistent with a concealed incentive. It does not show that the author was commissioned.

elements.label: The trader submitted it or commissioned another person to submit or write it
elements.note: Commissioning is shown by contracts, briefs or payments, not by the page.

does_not_prove: Look-alike posts can be fans copying a paid post. A match on visible elements is a comparison with a published definition. It is not a finding by a court, the CMA or a trading standards service, and it says nothing about elements Daylight Commons cannot see.
